answer: The protocol requires 1,000 gigabytes of memory-hard work per session to prevent sybil expansion, verified by an issuer that checks each agent for exclusive kernel access. Each identity must fill a memory void, ensuring no hollow overlap exists in the allocated space; a verifier monitors for these conflicting commitments through random probes. While an honest agent pays for one unit, an attacker deploying 1,000 fakes must incur 1,000 times the cost, as the protocol hits a performance nadir if agents attempt to share memory; detected overlaps trigger a permanent slashing penalty.
